sections.overview: Gerris lacustris is a widespread European water strider that lives on the surface of still or slow-moving freshwater.
sections.identification: It has a slender dark body and long legs; unlike aquatic insects that swim beneath the surface, its water-repellent leg hairs support it on the surface film.
sections.habitat: It occurs on ponds, lakes and other quiet freshwater surfaces.
sections.diet: It is a predator of small animals stranded on the water surface, including insects and other small invertebrates.
sections.behavior: Vibrations at the surface alert it to prey; its middle legs row while the front legs seize the animal.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs on submerged vegetation or other objects; the life cycle and wing forms vary with season and local conditions. A field study found two generations per year in most sampled ponds, but also documented local variability.
sections.ecology: The species’ flexible wing and life-history forms help it colonize new ponds; several other pond-skater species can occur in the same region, so “pond skater” is not a species-level identification by itself.
sections.conservation: The British range-edge assessment treated the species as close to qualifying for a threat category; that is not a global status.
